related_questions.question: What is the maximum you can borrow on an FHA loan?

text_blocks.snippet: In 2025, the maximum FHA loan amount for a single-family home is $524,225 in most areas. However, in high-cost areas, the maximum can be up to $1,209,750 for a single-family home. The specific limit also depends on the number of units in the property and the location (county).

list.title: Standard Areas:
list.snippet: The standard FHA loan limit for a single-family home is $524,225.

list.title: High-Cost Areas:
list.snippet: In designated high-cost areas, the limit for a single-family home can be as high as $1,209,750.

list.title: Multi-Family Properties:
list.snippet: FHA loan limits increase for multi-unit properties (2-4 units). For example, in standard areas, the limit for a two-unit property is $671,200, and for a four-unit property, it's $1,008,300, according to Neighbors Bank.

list.title: Location Matters:
list.snippet: FHA loan limits are determined by median home prices in each county and are adjusted annually.

text_blocks.snippet: To find the exact limit for your specific location, you can:

list.snippet: Use the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) website (HUD.gov) to search by state or county.
Consult with a mortgage lender specializing in FHA loans.
